title: Becoming a film editor
summary: He started editing newsreels in Philadelphia, moved to New York industrial films and features, and describes working with directors.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: When did you get into movie work?
And, did you start out as an editor, movie editor?
Yes, I started out editing newsreels in a television station in Philadelphia. I went down there for a year.
And, how did that happen to lead into your presence, actually?

Well, I decided there were more opportunities for film editors in New York. And, I came back to New York and I got a job for a producer of industrial films. I did that for a few years, commercials and things like that. And, now I work on feature films.
In the editing, are you called upon to make decisions yourself on what will be included in the...
Yes, constantly you're making decisions. Small ones, but it's the sum of many small decisions that build the picture.
Who do you work most closely with in this? The producer?
The director. The director. Yes. I guess the director. Yes. In fact, the editing is actually an extension of the work that the director does.
So, do you spend a lot of your time editing at his side?

Well, I mean, he doesn't actually spend a great deal of time in the cutting room. I mean, he doesn't stand over your shoulder and tell you where to cut, but he looks at the work you've done every day or every couple of days or maybe once a week, depending on a lot of things. And, he will make suggestions and tell you what he thinks is wrong with the sequence and ask you to rework it and look for... Try to emphasize certain aspects of the scene and de-emphasize others. It's a process of trial and error.
